note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 1 June 1961 (Notice of Election, Fermanagh Herald, 6 May 1961, p. 2). No division was contested: the Belfast Telegraph of 31 May 1961, p. 2, states that there were 'no contests in Co. Tyrone or for Fermanagh County Council', so all twenty members were returned at the nominations. The Belfast News-Letter of 17 May 1961, p. 5, names the only two changes: 'Mr. Curry succeeds Mr. Cahir Healy, M.P., and Mr. Loane succeeds Mr. J. Orr.' Healy had sat for Crum since the by-election of February 1958, following the death of Mr. James Goodwin (Belfast News-Letter, 20 February 1958, p. 4), so Curry is recorded for Crum; Orr held Enniskillen Rural in 1958, so Loane is recorded there. The paper says there were two new members only; the other members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the earlier returns. Brookeborough, Laragh, Lisbellaw, Maguiresbridge and Monea are filled (6 Nov 2026) from the Impartial Reporter's report of Unionist selections of 11 May 1961, p. 5; its nominations report of 18 May 1961, p. 7, confirms no contest and only two changes on the county council. Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Doon, Innismacsaint, Irvinestown, Derrylea and Roslea. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Lisnaskea, Enniskillen Borough, Florencecourt and Ballinamallard. Returned unopposed.
